notes:
Account snapshot: SealGuard DevTools is an enterprise healthcare platform that builds developer tooling (IDE plugins, internal code search, CI linters) for clinical software teams. They need an enterprise-grade code assistant that can run in a private VPC or fully on-prem (air-gapped) with SSO/SAML, tamper-evident audit logs, and configurable retention for PHI-related artifacts.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-01-10: Intro call (AE Ethan Park) — overview of Redwood dedicated/private options; customer: "we cannot send PHI off network".
- 2026-01-15: Security deep-dive with SecOps (Fireflies ff_2026-01-15_84921) — asked for encryption-at-rest proof, KMS integration, and runtime attestations.
- 2026-01-28: Demo of hosted API + latency benchmarks (50ms median for single-token streaming in lab). Customer concerned about network egress and model pinning.
- 2026-02-03: SE workshop (Maya) — walked through model version pinning, rollout policies, and canary fallback to quantized variant.
- 2026-02-20: POC kickoff call (Fireflies ff_2026-02-20_99213) — Secure tunnel to their lab for a 2-week low-latency streaming pilot; initial integration into VSCode plugin prototype.
- 2026-02-25: POC interim: streaming completions stable at ~60ms median in lab when pinned to a trimmed context model; embedding latency acceptable but throughput needs batching improvements. SE suggested Optimize recommendations for batching and KV caching.

Use-case & requirements summary:
- Primary: IDE copilot for clinical engineers (auto-complete, function suggestions, code explainers tied to internal repos).
- Targets: median completion latency <100ms for single-line suggestions, 2000 requests/min sustained during internal hackathons, support for streaming partial tokens to IDE plugin.
- Model requirements: ability to pin exact model + quantization variant per environment; deterministic rollbacks; fallback chains (primary high-quality model -> low-cost quantized model -> local cached completions).
- Security/compliance: SSO/SAML integration with Okta, full audit trails for every completion request, configurable retention policy (90d for dev logs; 7 years for audit records per clinical compliance), KMS/HSM-backed key management, EU/US data residency options.

Open items and blockers:
- Legal needs specific PHI handling language in SOW; security team requested SOC2 Type II + ISO27001 artifacts.
- Internal schedule conflict: migration to company-wide SAML provider planned for Q3 — impacts timing for full rollout.
- Cost sensitivity: prefer a predictable committed tier for Dedicated with ordered burst capacity; procurement wants two pricing options.

Quoted feedback from the technical lead: "We need completions that feel native in VSCode — streaming + predictable latency is non-negotiable. If we can prove on-prem parity with hosted latency, procurement will move fast."

Documents referenced: security FAQ (drive link), draft SOW (drive), POC notes (JIRA SEC-4321), benchmarking notebook attached to INF-1197.

Next tactical steps: SE to deliver Optimize config for POC (batching + KV settings); schedule on-prem pilot install window; AE to coordinate legal on PHI language and present two committed-tier pricing scenarios.
